technical_decisions.title: An unseeded identifier scope is isolated (DET-007)
technical_decisions.problem: id_scope(None) returned a null context, so a run started without a seed inside a seeded scope drew its identifiers from that scope's stream: the enclosing run's later identifiers depended on whether, and how much, a nested run had drawn.
technical_decisions.alternatives: (a) Keep inheriting and document it. (b) An unseeded scope installs its own uuid4 source. (c) An unseeded scope derives a child stream from the enclosing one.
technical_decisions.decision: (b): id_scope(None) installs use_id_source(id_source(None)), a uuid4 source of its own.
technical_decisions.rationale: A scope must draw nothing from the scope around it. (c) still advances or depends on the outer stream; (a) leaves a seeded run's identifiers hostage to unrelated code.
technical_decisions.compatibility: A seeded run's identifiers are unchanged, and the enclosing scope now mints exactly what it would have without the nested run. An unseeded run's identifiers were never reproducible. No recorded result_id, configuration_id, schema or format moves; the certificate's evidence is unchanged.
technical_decisions.record: CHANGELOG [4.3.0] Fixed; the ledger, once the package version admits v4.3.0 entries.
technical_decisions.tests: tests/regression/test_unseeded_scopes_are_isolated.py (backtest, replay and session drivers; nested, repeated, fresh-interpreter and parallel copy_context probes); mutation K01.

technical_decisions.title: Registries derive their identifiers (DET-007, plan D-54-7)
technical_decisions.problem: experiment_tracking.start_run and cloud_research.submit_research_job drew their identifiers from the ambient stream, so starting a run or queuing a job inside a seeded backtest moved that backtest's stream, and neither identifier could be recomputed from what was declared.
technical_decisions.alternatives: (a) A dedicated seeded stream per registry. (b) uuid5 over a canonical, scheme-tagged key of the declaration and its place in the registry (ADR-0016's pattern). (c) A content hash of the declaration alone.
technical_decisions.decision: (b), with schemes alphalab.experiment_run.v1 and alphalab.research_job.v1. A run's key holds its place (runs already held), name, canonical parameters, timestamp, parent and canonical tags. A job's key holds the cluster, its submission count, type, task path, priority and instant, and not its kwargs, which may be any objects with no canonical text.
technical_decisions.rationale: A derived identifier draws nothing and is recomputable anywhere. (c) collides when a declaration is repeated, and (a) still depends on the order in which unrelated registries are used.
technical_decisions.compatibility: New runs and jobs get UUID strings as before, now derived; identifiers already recorded are read as written. No recorded result_id, configuration_id, schema or format moves.
technical_decisions.record: CHANGELOG [4.3.0] Fixed; the ledger, once the package version admits v4.3.0 entries.
technical_decisions.tests: tests/regression/test_registries_derive_their_ids.py (12 tests); stress scenario registries (stress_v4_3.py); mutations K02 to K05.

technical_decisions.title: The HTTP transport opens http and https only (SEC-002)

technical_decisions.decision: (b), with https requests carrying tls_context().
technical_decisions.rationale: (a) leaves the file read open. (c) refuses loopback and plain-http providers that the transport legitimately serves.
technical_decisions.compatibility: A caller passing another scheme now gets an error before anything is opened. Reading another scheme was never a stated capability (SECURITY.md stated TLS only), so nothing documented changes.

technical_decisions.title: A release is developed under its own version
technical_decisions.problem: From M1 the programme changes the public API and records v4.3 findings, and the records that take them are keyed to the package version: the manifest and its history copy, the certificate, and the ledger guard. Since v4.2.1 the suite also held every commit to the release state. At 4.2.1, an API change would have rewritten history/4.2.1.json, the record of what 4.2.1 shipped, and a 4.3 ledger entry fails the guard.
technical_decisions.alternatives: (a) Stay at 4.2.1 and bump at the end, with gates red or records wrong meanwhile. (b) A PEP 440 development version, 4.3.0.dev0; every gate, artifact name and tag check assumes MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. (c) 4.3.0 everywhere at once; the README and INTEGRATION would name a current release, and download URLs, that do not exist until publication. (d) 4.3.0 in an explicit development state.
technical_decisions.decision: (d). The package and its records are 4.3.0, and the CHANGELOG leads with '# [4.3.0] - Unreleased'. release_preflight.development_problems (run by the suite) holds the tree to everything a release is held to but that heading's date, and the documents a reader installs from describe 4.2.1, the newest dated release, until the release commit. The release gate (release_preflight.py version) is unchanged and refuses the tree for the undated heading.
technical_decisions.rationale: Every commit stays green and truthful, and the gate that matters is untouched. No document ever names a release that cannot be installed, and no line calls 4.3.0 unreleased (DOC-013). The release commit is one explicit step that the suite verifies.
technical_decisions.compatibility: No identity moves: the engine keeps its version out of every identity, and the certificate moved only its release labels, its source digest and API-1's digest of the manifest file. running_engine() and dataset provenance record 4.3.0 for runs this tree makes, which is true. Preflight.yml expects 4.3.0, and its push route names work/v4.3.0-release; the development branch never triggers it (D-W1).

technical_decisions.title: ADR-0053 revision 3: where a continuation is held to its schedule
technical_decisions.problem: R53-1 asks for a supplied schedule digest on run_snapshot.restore and restore_checkpoints, as FUT-041 does for the registry. A bare run snapshot records no binding, so the parameter would have nothing to check there, and a caller could believe a continuation was held to its schedule when it was not. A bare digest also drops the scheme it was computed under.
technical_decisions.alternatives: (a) Add schedule_digest to both restores, as written; on a bare snapshot it checks nothing. (b) Hold a chain by its own envelope (checkpoint schema 3), and a bare snapshot by the cursor given the binding its provenance records; pass a ScheduleBinding, not a digest. (c) Put the binding into the run snapshot; this moves identity, which is option B, 5.0.
technical_decisions.decision: (b): ScheduleCursor.start(expected=), checkpoint(schedule=) and restore_checkpoints(schedule_binding=) take a ScheduleBinding, and run_snapshot.restore gains nothing. VERIFIED needs a result whose own delivery record is read; a payload's or a chain's check answers DECLARED. ScheduleBinding and ScheduleVerification live in alphalab.runtime, beside RegistryVerification, since a checkpoint (runtime) records a binding and runtime may not import backtesting.
technical_decisions.rationale: Every check named is one that actually happens, the scheme is compared with the digest, and no package edge is added.
technical_decisions.compatibility: Additive only: keyword-only parameters defaulting to None on checkpoint, restore_checkpoints and ScheduleCursor.start. Version-2 chains are byte-identical and restore as before. No identity moves.

technical_decisions.title: Manifest provenance: what identity version 2 records, and where the unattested finding belongs
technical_decisions.problem: Three questions were left open. (1) D-53-3 asks for 'unchanged behaviour plus a finding' when no provenance is given, but a version-1 manifest can never cite provenance, so the finding would land on every manifest ever made, changing every assessment. (2) ADR-0052's migration step refused instruments=False under version 2, and instruments defaults to False, so a refusal cannot be told apart from the default. (3) Provenance carries the result id, an output; comparing it as an input would report a rerun that did not reproduce as one whose inputs differ.
technical_decisions.alternatives: (1) The finding on every manifest without provenance; only under version 2; or none. (2) Refuse instruments=False under version 2, or record the registry under version 2 whatever instruments says. (3) Compare provenance_id between original and rerun, or compare only the inputs it binds -- the schedule's and the registry's digests, which are already compared.
technical_decisions.decision: (1) The finding only under version 2, the contract that asks for provenance. (2) Version 2 records the registry the run held whatever instruments says. (3) provenance_id is not an input; a version-2 rerun of a version-1 original is compared by version 1's rules, and a detail line says so.
technical_decisions.rationale: Version-1 manifests, their assessments and the certificate's evidence stay exactly as they were (CR-53-7, CR-53-8). A version-2 producer is told what it did not attest, and an outcome names what actually differed.
technical_decisions.compatibility: Version 1 is unchanged in identity, verification, gaps and findings; version 2 is opt-in. ReproducibilityManifest, canonical_manifest_key and derive_manifest_id gain trailing fields and parameters with defaults, rendered only when given. A version-1 manifest is also stored as v4.2.1 stored it: ReproducibilityManifest projects without the two new fields while they hold their defaults, because an evidence store refuses another value under an identity it holds (the frozen v4.2.1 evidence store's test found the first draft writing them).
technical_decisions.record: docs/ADR/0053-run-and-input-provenance.md section 6; docs/ADR/0052 (status: accepted, option C, opt-in); CHANGELOG [4.3.0].
technical_decisions.tests: tests/integration/test_manifest_provenance.py (12 tests); tests/regression/test_schema_upgrades_v4_2_1.py::test_the_evidence_store_reads_back_verified_and_this_build_computes_the_same.

technical_decisions.title: Provenance refuses a binding of no schedule for a run that delivered observations
technical_decisions.problem: The delivery-record rule (REP-009) checks observations only when a schedule is named, because a manifest naming none for such a run has never been refused. Read the same way, forged provenance binding no schedule verified NONE_GIVEN for a run that delivered observations.
technical_decisions.alternatives: (a) Tighten the shared rule, which refuses a manifest_for_run call that succeeds today, a change in what a valid call computes. (b) A stricter rule for provenance alone, which is new API. (c) Leave it, and let NONE_GIVEN mean less than it says.
technical_decisions.decision: (b): run_provenance and verify_provenance refuse a binding of no schedule for a run whose record shows delivered observations; manifests keep the 4.x rule.
technical_decisions.rationale: The vocabulary must never claim more than the run's record allows, and an existing call's result must not change in a minor release.
technical_decisions.compatibility: No existing call changes; provenance is new in v4.3.

technical_decisions.title: ADR-0058: host independence by construction, not by rounding
technical_decisions.problem: Plan section H.1 proposed recording identity-bearing statistics as decimal strings rounded to twelve significant digits, so hosts whose libm differs in the last bit would agree. The owner's direction for G0 item 24 forbids arbitrary fixed rounding that conceals numerical differences, and rounding cannot make two hosts agree anyway: values a last bit apart that straddle a rounding boundary round to different strings at any number of digits.
technical_decisions.alternatives: (a) Twelve significant digits, as H.1 proposed. (b) Fewer digits, chosen per statistic, with the same boundary failure. (c) Three classes of result -- exact, correctly rounded, host libm -- with identities allowed over the first two only, every value recorded at full precision, class-3 values compared by tolerances derived from error analysis, and host independence proved by pinned reference tests on Linux and macOS.
technical_decisions.decision: (c), with the transcendental an identity needs computed on an exact or correctly rounded path instead, such as the stationary bootstrap's block lengths by integer comparison of hash-counter draws.
technical_decisions.rationale: It follows item 24's direction exactly, extends what REP-005 already does for run records, and makes cross-host equality a property a test proves rather than an outcome a rounding hopes for.
technical_decisions.compatibility: No existing identity or figure moves; LIM-005 stays a stated limitation, now a named class with a rule.
technical_decisions.record: docs/ADR/0058-numerical-foundation-host-independence-and-the-identity-of-an-estimate.md; plan change PC-02's reading of AC-37.
technical_decisions.tests: Each M2 module's pinned reference tests on CI's Linux and macOS cells (built in M2).

technical_decisions.title: ADR-0054: where the selection statistics live, and the bounds their required arguments take
technical_decisions.problem: R54-8 makes CSCV's S and the bootstrap's block length required and bounded, without saying how; the draft placed the statistics in research but left their numerical class and their bounds open.
technical_decisions.alternatives: (a) Defaults for S, q and B, which the draft's review refused. (b) Required arguments, unbounded. (c) Required arguments with stated bounds: S even, 2 <= S <= T and S <= 20 (C(20, 10) = 184,756 combinations), trimming of T declared; q >= 1, B >= 1 and the seed required; the adjusted PSR's lag count required.
technical_decisions.decision: (c), with the statistics pure in alphalab.research over common only, bootstrap positions from a hash-counter stream (class 1), p-values as exact fractions, RC, SPA and PBO class 2, and PSR, DSR, MinTRL and the adjusted PSR class 3, never in an identity.
technical_decisions.rationale: A bound makes a required argument's cost and meaning explicit; S above 20 makes CSCV's combinations impractical in pure Python, and nothing about the method needs more.
technical_decisions.compatibility: Additive: new modules and names; the existing PSR, DSR, expected maximum Sharpe and multiple-testing corrections unchanged.
technical_decisions.record: docs/ADR/0054-selection-statistics-measuring-a-search-over-backtests.md.

technical_decisions.title: The core's linear algebra: one Cholesky, QL for the eigensystem, Jacobi for the SVD, and their conventions
technical_decisions.problem: ADR-0058 makes common.linalg the one authority for a symmetric eigensystem and a thin SVD with vectors, Cholesky and a pseudo-inverse, with caller tolerances (section 2) and class-2 arithmetic for anything that may enter an identity (section 3). The constrained optimizer's private Cholesky had to move without moving a portfolio, the plan budgets a 500 x 500 eigensystem at 30 s in pure Python, and the conventions every caller relies on were open: which triangle of a symmetric matrix is read, the sign of a vector, what a result says about its convergence.
technical_decisions.alternatives: Eigensystem: (a) cyclic Jacobi, accurate to high relative precision on graded matrices with one global stopping criterion, measured at 147.5 s for 500 x 500; (b) Householder tridiagonalization and implicit QL (tql2), backward stable with orthonormal vectors, measured at 20.7 s. SVD: one-sided Jacobi, or Golub-Kahan bidiagonalization and implicit QR. Cholesky: a new factorization, or the optimizer's moved verbatim. Symmetry: refuse an asymmetric input exactly, refuse it beyond a tolerance, or read one triangle as LAPACK does.
technical_decisions.decision: (b) for the eigensystem, with the split criterion |e_m| <= tolerance (|d_m| + |d_m+1|) and max_iterations per eigenvalue, both required; one-sided Jacobi for the SVD (max_sweeps required), whose accuracy the plan sets no budget against; the optimizer's Cholesky moved verbatim, quadratic._cholesky delegating and Black-Litterman calling it directly, the private solve removed; the lower triangle read; each eigenvector and right singular vector with its largest-magnitude component positive, the left vector following; a ConvergenceReport on every iterative result; + - * /, sqrt and fsum only, after an exact power-of-two scaling, with no math.hypot or pow in the new code.
technical_decisions.rationale: Only (b) meets the plan's budget, and its accuracy is the normwise accuracy every caller of an eigensystem relies on. The SVD keeps Jacobi's relative accuracy, and its cost is stated (240.8 s at 500 x 500) with speed left to the optional backends (ADR-0057, LIM-010). Reading one triangle is the convention every library uses and the one the optimizer's factorization already had, which Black-Litterman's view system, symmetric only to rounding, depends on; an exact refusal would have broken it, and a tolerance would be a policy nobody chose. A fixed sign makes a result reproducible bit for bit, so it can be pinned and, as a class-2 value, enter an estimate's identity.
technical_decisions.compatibility: Additive. No public name is removed; the optimizer's private _cholesky keeps its name and _cholesky_solve, private, is gone. Every factor, pivot ratio and solve is v4.2.1's float for float, so no portfolio, result_id or figure moves. alphalab.common exports one new name, ConvergenceReport (API manifest 2,800 to 2,801 exports). ADR-0058's class-2 row now names math.hypot, which CPython computes itself, held by a pinned test.

technical_decisions.title: Optimisers and quadrature: which algorithms, what a caller must state, and the gradient check left in place
technical_decisions.problem: ADR-0058 section 1 names common.optimize (Nelder-Mead, BFGS, L-BFGS-B, Brent, golden section, numerical gradients) and common.quadrature (adaptive Gauss-Kronrod) as new authorities, with every answer-deciding choice required (section 2). Open were the line search, how each method states its criterion, what happens when double precision cannot meet a tolerance, and an existing public central difference in deep_learning.
technical_decisions.alternatives: Line search: Armijo backtracking, strong Wolfe (Nocedal and Wright 3.5/3.6), or Hager-Zhang's approximate Wolfe conditions, which resolve smaller gradients by trusting derivatives where values round. L-BFGS-B: the full method of Byrd, Lu, Nocedal and Zhu, or a projected L-BFGS under its name. Quadrature: QAG (adaptive Gauss-Kronrod 7-15) or QAGS with Wynn's epsilon extrapolation. Precision limits: return the last iterate with a flag, or raise. The deep-learning gradient: delegate to the new authority, or keep it as a recorded namesake.
technical_decisions.decision: Strong Wolfe with bisection zoom and stated constants (1e-4, 0.9, 60 trials); the full L-BFGS-B, its history size required; QAG without extrapolation, the rule's constants verified for exactness rather than trusted; a precision limit raises ConvergenceError with what was reached; the deep-learning check kept with its figures, recorded in PERMITTED_NAMESAKES and argued in test_shared_names_stay_distinct.py, its deprecation added to GAP-48 for 5.0.
technical_decisions.rationale: Strong Wolfe is the standard a reader can check and guarantees the curvature BFGS needs; approximate Wolfe would accept steps the values cannot show to decrease, which is a best effort by another name. A method named L-BFGS-B must be that method. QAG's estimate is the one QUADPACK users know; extrapolation can be added under its own name. Raising on a precision limit is ADR-0058's rule: the caller learns the tolerance their problem supports. The gradient check's figures underpin every layer's tests, and its loose comparison never needed more accuracy.
technical_decisions.compatibility: Additive: two new modules, no name removed or rebound, no figure moved. deep_learning.numerical_gradient unchanged.

technical_decisions.title: Selection statistics: exact where they count, and the conventions each states
technical_decisions.problem: ADR-0054 fixes the statistics and their required, bounded arguments; open were how ties are ranked, how a p-value counts, how the bootstrap draws without libm, how SPA's consistent threshold and PBO's logits avoid it, and what the autocorrelation adjustment is precisely.
technical_decisions.alternatives: Ranks: ordinal with an index tie-break, or midranks. p-values: #{V* > V}/B, #{V* >= V}/B, or (1 + #)/(1 + B). Bootstrap draws: random.Random, or a hash counter with u mod T, or with rejection. Thresholds and logits: math.log (class 3), or Decimal's correctly rounded ln. Adjustment: Lo's effective sample size, or the delta method over Newey-West long-run covariances of the mean and variance moments.
technical_decisions.decision: Midranks, with PBO counting 2r <= N + 1 as an integer comparison and the logits from Decimal ln; p = #{statistic* >= statistic}/B as an exact Fraction (White's count; conservative at an exact tie, and SPA's floor at 0 then gives p = 1 when no model beats the benchmark); SHA-256 counter draws with exact continuation by u q_num < 2^64 q_den and uniform starts by rejection; SPA's sqrt(2 ln ln T / T) by Decimal; the adjustment as Opdyke's independent variance plus Bartlett-weighted lag terms of the standardized mean and variance moments, which is the independent PSR exactly at lags = 0; the mean compared by its exactly rounded sum.
technical_decisions.rationale: Each choice keeps the result's class as ADR-0054 section 6 states it: integers and exact fractions where a count or a rank decides, correctly rounded arithmetic elsewhere, libm only where the normal distribution is the statistic. Reducing to the existing PSR at no lags means the adjustment changes nothing a caller already relies on.

technical_decisions.title: Global day counts: which bases, and how a basis gets what only its instrument knows
technical_decisions.problem: GAP-36: the library's day counts were the US and money-market three, and ADR-0039 kept 30E/360 and ACT/ACT ISDA out because their correct form depends on the instrument's terms. Several of the world's conventions cannot be computed from two dates alone: ICMA needs the coupon period and frequency, 30E/360 (ISDA) the termination date, BUS/252 a business calendar. Daily accruals on the run path divide a day's count by the basis's year, which three of them do not have.
technical_decisions.alternatives: (a) Bases computable from dates only, the rest left out. (b) Every basis, inferring the missing terms (a regular schedule, a default calendar, the end date as termination). (c) Every basis, with the instrument's terms passed explicitly, refused when missing and refused when given but unused; the variable-year bases computed as exact rationals; run-path accruals limited to the bases that weight a day alone.
technical_decisions.decision: (c): DayCountTerms, keyword-only on year_fraction and day_count_days; required_terms names what each basis takes; days_in_year refuses ACT/ACT (ISDA), ACT/ACT (ICMA) and ACT/365L; require_accrual_basis admits ACT/365F, ACT/360, 30/360, 30E/360 and NL/365, and financing and borrow terms call it at construction; the bond passes its own coupon period, frequency and maturity; ICMA and ACT/365L require the accrual to lie within its stated period, ICMA's notional periods for irregular coupons staying the schedule's own.
technical_decisions.rationale: ADR-0039's rule is that a convention is never defaulted. Inferring a coupon period or a calendar would reproduce the silent assumption the record removed; requiring them keeps every basis exact by its definition. Refusing an unused term catches a caller who believes it mattered. Refusing at construction moves a failure from mid-run to configuration.
technical_decisions.compatibility: Additive: seven DayCount members appended (existing members, their values and names unchanged); a keyword-only terms argument defaulting to None; three new names in alphalab.conventions (API manifest 2,821 exports). The three existing bases compute exactly what they did, so no accrual, run, result_id or persisted format moves.

technical_decisions.title: ADR-0055: a captured run beside run, an extractor whose every choice is stated, and a trace retention cannot move
technical_decisions.problem: Plan K.1: retention trims the equity curve, digest_run costs 62-69 % of a full-history run, retention changes result_id, and nothing observes a run, so a search of thousands of trials cannot get the TrialMatrix ADR-0054 takes without keeping every run whole and digesting it.
technical_decisions.alternatives: (a) A flag on BacktestEngine.run returning a wider type. (b) An observer callback the drivers call. (c) A separate run_captured over the drivers' one private step loop, returning the unchanged result beside a CaptureRecord. For the trace: (i) the digest of the kept record, which retention moves; (ii) a chain over each step's economic deltas, read before retention can lose them. For precision: (x) the plan K.1 text's rounding per H.1; (y) full precision under ADR-0058.
technical_decisions.decision: (c), (ii) and (y). CaptureSpec(extractor, trace) with every extractor choice required -- grid (EVERY_INSTANT or FixedInterval), costs (NET or GROSS), cash_flows (INCLUDED or EXCLUDED), currency (the run's base), insolvency (REFUSE or TRUNCATE); CaptureRecord with extractor_id, the series at full precision, series_id, trace_id and counts; the trace chained from the run's configuration_id over each step's new fills, ledger transactions, OMS order events and equity points, read as the change in each log's total appended (length plus dropped), refusing a bound smaller than one step's output; RetentionPolicy.keep_equity, written only when true; lifecycle.selection's bridge from captures to a TrialMatrix.
technical_decisions.rationale: A separate function keeps run's four overloads and every return type as they are (R53-3). An EVERY_INSTANT, NET, INCLUDED series is analytics' own arithmetic, so M3's exit gate -- a 16-variant PBO from captures equal to one from full history -- holds by construction rather than by tolerance. Reading deltas from the logs' dropped counts makes the trace retention-independent without a hook inside the step.
technical_decisions.compatibility: Additive: new names only, one defaulted RetentionPolicy field written only when true; no result_id, configuration_id, manifest_id, digest or format moves. Departures from plan K.1's text: full precision (ADR-0058, PC-02), and the calendar-session grid waits for ADR-0059's packs.

technical_decisions.title: ADR-0059: membership dated twice, read through the registry as known, a survivorship control caught by its trades, and a pack format

How it is dated: (i) effective dates; (ii) effective and announcement instants. How survivorship is caught: (x) a score over returns, which RES-001 removed; (y) a review naming the trades made outside membership as it was known.
technical_decisions.decision: (c), (ii) and (y). MembershipChange(universe, asset_id, kind ADDITION/REMOVAL/DELISTING, effective_at, announced_at <= effective_at); HistoricalUniverse refusing inconsistent histories and retroactive announcements; members(at, as_of) reading only what was announced by as_of; context.universe.members(universe, at) with as_of the context's instant; the registry's digest covering universes only when present; research.bias.membership_review; data.packs.ReferencePack with source, as_of, validity, licence, typed entries and a content digest under alphalab.reference_pack.v1, refusing a mismatched digest, a query outside its range and a missing entry.

technical_decisions.title: ADR-0055 at implementation: a trace from the configuration kept whole, bookings met by operation, GROSS and EXCLUDED exactly, and a canonical writer
technical_decisions.problem: Implementing ADR-0055 showed three gaps. Its trace started from the run's configuration_id, which covers the retention policy, so the trace could not be equal across retentions as section 5 requires. The run keeps equity points and bookings in separate logs, several of each a step, so GROSS and EXCLUDED had no exact way to know which bookings a point shows. And the trace's serialization through serialize cost 28 percent of a run.
technical_decisions.alternatives: The trace's start: (a) the run's configuration_id; (b) the configuration with its retention set aside; (c) no configuration at all. Placing a booking: (i) by its own timestamp, wrong under latency, where a fill is stamped after the event that books it, and for child fills booked after the record's point; (ii) by the operation that booked it, observed after every operation. The serialization: (x) serialize, per step; (y) a per-type writer producing serialize's text byte for byte.
technical_decisions.decision: (b), with the record's configuration_id the run's own; (ii), with a refusal if one operation records equity at two instants under GROSS or EXCLUDED; and (y), held to serialize by the pinned identities, computed with serialize before the writer existed. GROSS adds back the valuation's own commission_paid at each point, which is a fill's commission, fees and tax. EXCLUDED removes CashFlowBooked, CashDeposited and CashWithdrawn amounts, never a conversion's legs, converted at the closing point's rates. TRUNCATE keeps the return into the first insolvent instant. The trace reads its logs once a step.
technical_decisions.rationale: A retention decides what a run keeps, not what it does. Every operation books before the point it records, so an operation is the finest unit at which a booking's point is known, and the schedule cursor's loop already applies one entry at a time. Each adjustment is held to a counterfactual run exactly. The writer's text is serialize's, so the trace's canonical form stays the repository's one form.
technical_decisions.compatibility: No identity moves for any run: the step loop and the cursor's loop are the ones run took, with no observer given; the full suite and every frozen replay are unchanged. _recorded_configuration moved from the lifecycle to runtime.run_snapshot unchanged.

technical_decisions.title: ADR-0059 at implementation: a pack's format in data, its meaning in instrument; bounded universes; what a view without a registry answers
technical_decisions.problem: ADR-0059 put typed MembershipChange entries in data.packs, but the data package may reach nothing on the execution path: tests/regression/test_import_graph_stays_acyclic.py pins its outward edges to common and options. And a universe built from a pack would lose the pack's range and knowledge, so its refusals would not hold inside a run.
technical_decisions.alternatives: The pack's types: (a) widen the data package's edges to instrument and persistence; (b) hold entries as records tagged with their type in data, typed by the instrument package; (c) move packs out of data. The pack's bounds: (i) checked on the pack only; (ii) carried by the universe built from it.
technical_decisions.decision: (b) and (ii). data.packs holds the format and the checks that need only the pack -- tagged records held to their type's shape, the digest over canonical JSON, the range, the announcement horizon, the missing universe. instrument.membership.universe_from_pack reads the entries into a HistoricalUniverse that takes optional coverage and known_until and refuses a query outside either. UniverseView.members and NoUniverse.members answer no members without a registry, as every universe answer does; a registry without the named universe refuses. register_universe refuses a member the registry does not hold.
technical_decisions.rationale: The boundary that keeps the package graph acyclic is a stated rule, not a convenience. Meaning belongs to the domain that has it. A refusal that held only on the pack would be lost the moment the pack's universe entered the registry.
technical_decisions.compatibility: Additive. A registry without universes snapshots and digests byte for byte as v4.2.1 wrote it (InstrumentRegistrySnapshot.universes is written only when one is carried); the frozen fixtures and pinned registry digests are unchanged.

technical_decisions.title: ADR-0072 at implementation: a dataset held by its record digest, diagnostics outside every identity, the outcome rules, statistics at M5
technical_decisions.problem: Building the ledger showed four places the ADR's text needed settling: a MarketDataset carries no source content hash for a manifest's dataset fields; a failed trial's error text differs between interpreter versions, which would make one experiment's record differ across hosts and a resume elsewhere look nondeterministic; the outcome of a runner's error, of inputs that are not the experiment's and of recorded strategy failures needed rules; and the plan's milestone table places the ledger's statistics at M5.
technical_decisions.alternatives: Dataset identity: the manifest's version and content hash, or the record digest replay already uses. Diagnostics: in the identity, out of it, or not kept. Statistics: in M4's record, or M5's.
technical_decisions.decision: dataset_identity is the dataset's id and dataset_digest. Diagnostics are kept with the first record and enter neither record_id, experiment_record_id nor the nondeterminism check. A runner raising AlphaLab's error is REFUSED, any other FAILED; inputs not the experiment's are REFUSED, naming the part; a run with recorded strategy failures is STRATEGY_FAILED with its identities. The ledger sets each run's seed and retention. TrialLimits holds only a time limit. M4's ExperimentRecord holds counts and the completed trials' matrix_id; DSR, SPA and PBO over it are M5's.
technical_decisions.rationale: Every trial can be held to the digest of the records it ran over. A record that differed only in an interpreter's wording would make O.3's cross-host requirement unmeetable for any experiment with a failure. The outcome rules follow ADR-0072's table: what is AlphaLab's refusal is REFUSED, what is the researcher's code is FAILED or STRATEGY_FAILED.

technical_decisions.title: One registry in alphalab.common, and the research cluster as one of the ledger's executors (GAP-05, GAP-31, D-54-6, D-54-11)
technical_decisions.problem: D-54-11 asks for one registry serving the ledger's executors and cloud_research, and GAP-31 for one executor path over distributed, cluster_scheduler and cloud_research. But cloud_research may not import lifecycle, which composes it, so the ledger's RunnerRegistry could not serve it. cloud_research's cycle hardcoded distributed's scheduler and dotted-path resolution, so cluster_scheduler's policies could run nothing, and the ledger could not run on a cluster.
technical_decisions.alternatives: The registry: keep it in lifecycle and give cloud_research a second one; a structural protocol; or move the one class below both, to alphalab.common. The cycle's registry path: new submission functions for registered tasks, or the job's task_path read as a registered name when the cycle is given a registry. The executor path: a ClusterExecutor driving distributed's state machine itself, which would copy the cycle; or one that runs trials as registered tasks on cloud_research's own cycle. The generic spawned worker moved into distributed, so that cluster tasks too would run in it.
technical_decisions.decision: RunnerRegistry moves to alphalab.common.registry, re-exported by alphalab.lifecycle, refusing with AlphaLabRegistryError. run_cluster_cycle gains keyword-only registry and assign: with a registry a job's task_path is a name looked up in it, and one it does not hold fails the job before anything is imported or submitted. assign is the AssignmentPolicy, so cluster_scheduler's aging and affinity policies run jobs. ClusterExecutor submits each trial to an idle cloud_research cluster as a registered task whose body spawns the trial's worker, and runs the cycle until every trial is done, yielding in submission order. resolve_task stays, superseded, until 5.0.
technical_decisions.rationale: One class is what lets one registry serve both, and common is the one package both may import. Reading task_path as a name keeps the job format and the sweep functions, so the cloud sweep runs through the registry unchanged and the 4.2.1 behaviour is the default. Running trials on the cycle itself makes it the one path: the scheduler's policies, distributed's job lifecycle and the spawned worker each do their part once. The worker stays in lifecycle: a registered cluster task runs in the executor the caller supplies, which BDY-028 already states.
technical_decisions.compatibility: Additive. run_cluster_cycle's new keywords default to its 4.2.1 behaviour; RunnerRegistry and the ledger are unreleased. lifecycle gains two edges, to cloud_research and distributed, which leave the standalone-engine list; nothing imports lifecycle.

technical_decisions.title: rerun_trial, an experiment that draws no identifier, and a time limit that times the trial
technical_decisions.problem: Reading WS-05 and GAP-01 against what M4 had delivered showed three things missing or wrong. GAP-01's acceptance and WS-05's item 14 ask that rerun_trial reproduce a record in a fresh process, and there was none. ADR-0054's review asks for zero identifier draws, and a sequential experiment drew 36 from a seeded scope around it -- four per trial whose runner built inputs, all of them the runner's, none the ledger's -- while a cluster's events drew from the caller's stream too. And M4's first mutation run caught every mutation through the time-limit tests, whatever the mutation: under its four parallel suites a spawned worker's start (0.46 s idle, about 1.15 s under load, against a 50 ms trial) outran the two-second limit, because the parent's timer counted the interpreter's start and its imports.
technical_decisions.alternatives: rerun_trial: filing the rerun's record (the ledger refuses a different one anyway) or reporting it. The runner's draws: an isolated uuid4 scope, or a scope seeded by the trial. The limit: a longer limit in the tests, which would hide the defect rather than remove it; the worker signalling when it has loaded so the parent's timer starts then; or the worker timing its own trial, with the parent keeping a start allowance as a backstop.
technical_decisions.decision: rerun_trial(spec, registry, runner, ledger, trial_id, executor) runs one recorded trial again and returns a TrialRerun holding the held and the rerun record ids; it files nothing. run_trial runs the runner in id_scope over the trial's own formula in a phase no trial has, and ClusterExecutor enters id_scope(None) around each of the cluster's calls, never across a yield. The worker starts a watchdog once it has loaded the experiment, and a trial still running at the limit ends the process with TIMED_OUT; the parent waits the limit plus a 600-second start allowance before treating a silent worker as dead.
technical_decisions.rationale: A rerun is a check, not a record. A seeded scope makes a runner's identifiers the trial's in every process and order -- the same reason a run mints from its seed -- and an isolated scope for the cluster keeps its bookkeeping out of the caller's stream. A researcher's limit is on their trial: a busy host slows an interpreter's start, and that must never interrupt a trial that runs in milliseconds. Measured: under sixteen busy processes and three concurrent suites the old code recorded 0 of 9 normal trials in each time-limit test, and the new code passes all three.
technical_decisions.compatibility: Additive (TrialRerun, rerun_trial); the ledger and its executors are unreleased. No record moved: the reference experiment's pinned identities hold, because a runner's identifiers do not enter its run's.

technical_decisions.title: Spawned workers serve many trials, as the researcher chooses, and an executor's cost is judged on one worker
technical_decisions.problem: WS-05 item 15 holds an executor's overhead to at most 5 percent of the summed trial time. SpawnExecutor started a fresh interpreter for every trial, and a start is about half a second -- 0.01 s of interpreter and 0.44 s of importing alphalab.lifecycle.experiments, which loads the lifecycle package -- so on 48 trials of about 0.6 s it cost 73 percent. Measuring four workers also showed what no executor controls: the same trials in four plain processes, with no executor, cost 10.1 percent more CPU than one, on a host of four performance and four efficiency cores.
technical_decisions.alternatives: Trimming AlphaLab's imports (any import of the ledger loads the lifecycle package, so not without restructuring it); a fork server (fork safety on macOS); workers that load the experiment once and serve trials one at a time, the fresh interpreter per trial kept as a choice. Judging the budget on four workers, which counts the host's slowdown as the executor's, or on one, which measures what the executor itself costs.
technical_decisions.decision: The worker reads a header naming the experiment, then one request per trial, and loads the definition once, behind the network refusal. SpawnExecutor(definition, workers, trials_per_worker) keeps one worker per pool thread: trials_per_worker is required, 1 for a fresh interpreter per trial and None for one per worker. A worker that ends interrupts its trial and a fresh one takes the next. Answers go to a duplicate of the standard output, which itself goes to the standard error. benchmarks/benchmark_experiments.py judges the executor's own cost on one worker reused against the plan's 5 percent, and prints a fresh interpreter per trial and four workers, with what each figure holds.
technical_decisions.rationale: A start paid once per worker is the cost the budget can bear; a researcher who wants every trial in a clean interpreter can still have it, at a start a trial. One worker measures the executor and nothing of the host. With W workers the cost is W starts and the exchanges, under 5 percent once each worker runs about ten seconds of trials; a trial of the plan's cost envelope (K.5) runs ten minutes.
technical_decisions.compatibility: SpawnExecutor gains a required field; it is unreleased. Records are unchanged under either lifetime, and spawned equals sequential record for record.
technical_decisions.record: docs/ADR/0072-experiments-and-the-trial-ledger.md (settled at implementation, points 8 and 14); SECURITY.md (BDY-029).
technical_decisions.tests: tests/integration/test_spawned_trials.py (every behaviour under both lifetimes; the starts counted); benchmarks/benchmark_experiments.py, judged by _stable_timing's method on a clock counting the workers' CPU, the collector running in both: one worker reused +2.1 percent (ok; 1.8 on single runs), a fresh interpreter per trial +73 to +80, four workers +20 to +28; the no-executor control +10.1.

technical_decisions.title: ADR-0073 accepted: validation over backtests, M5's entry condition
technical_decisions.problem: GAP-02: walk-forward, cross-validation and CPCV run on series, not on strategies, and ADR-0072's experiment has one design, the full sample. The plan (K.4, WS-24, N2, S-13) asks for designs in the specification, a declared warm-up never scored, fold-restricted runs, selection recorded as trials, CPCV paths, the ledger's statistics and a promotion method that leaves every evidence_id unchanged; it assigns the ADR no number.
technical_decisions.alternatives: Designs as a separate study object beside the experiment, or inside ExperimentSpec. Selection by the caller, or by the ledger as a recorded fact. CPCV's splits in lifecycle, or in research beside the other splitters. A trial's window passed to the runner to restrict, or the ledger restricting the run as it holds back a lockbox.
technical_decisions.decision: ExperimentSpec.validation takes FullSample, WalkForward, CrossValidated or CombinatorialPurged, every choice stated. Folds are research's splitters' over the dataset's instants, a new combinatorial_purged_splits among them. A trial is a candidate, a fold and a phase (SEARCH, SELECT, REPORT, VALIDATE, TEST) over a window the ledger restricts its run to, the warm-up run and never scored. The ledger selects and records the selection; run_experiment runs what a design names, then what a selection names. ExperimentRecord gains the selections, the out-of-sample series and the paths, written only when present. trial_matrix_of and assess_experiment read the ledger; ValidationMethod gains EXPERIMENT, and EXPERIMENT evidence must state its family count.
technical_decisions.rationale: A design is what a trial's result turns on, so it belongs where the experiment's identity covers it. A selection the caller makes is the leak the ledger exists to close. The split mathematics has one authority. Restricting the run in the ledger keeps a runner from seeing data a window may not.
technical_decisions.compatibility: Additive. A full-sample experiment's records and pinned identities are ADR-0072's; the new record fields are written only when present; the ValidationMethod member is appended.
technical_decisions.record: docs/ADR/0073-validation-over-backtests.md.
technical_decisions.tests: M5's: the leak mutants (purge boundary, embargo off, warm-up scored, lockbox reused) and S-13.

technical_decisions.title: The experiment assessment: each design's family, N, and members without a dispersion
technical_decisions.problem: ADR-0073 section 7 names trial_matrix_of(ledger, record), and the deflated Sharpe ratio with N the ledger's count of completed trials. But a record holds identities only, and a designed experiment's completed trials are the same candidates in every fold. Two of the statistics also divide by a member's dispersion. A candidate that never trades has none, and neither has a candidate measured against its own returns. Research refuses both: per_period_sharpe refuses returns without dispersion, and superior_predictive_ability refuses a model whose bootstrap deviation is zero. In the walk-forward reference experiment, the squeeze candidate's one trade precedes every window, so SPA against cash refused the whole assessment.
technical_decisions.alternatives: (a) Let the refusal stand. Then a search holding a candidate that never trades, measured against cash, has no assessment, and nor does one measured against a candidate's own returns, the benchmark section 7 names. (b) Give such a member a value: a Sharpe ratio or a studentized mean of 0 or of an infinity. Research defines these as undefined, not zero or infinite. Nor is the limit unique: a near-constant member's standardized bootstrap term stays of order one. (c) Make research's SPA accept a zero deviation. That changes ADR-0054's statistic and a refusal its tests pin. (d) Leave such a member out of each statistic that divides by its dispersion, name it, and report no statistic when fewer than two members remain.
technical_decisions.decision: (d). trial_matrix_of(spec, ledger, record, path=...) reads the family of at least two candidates. A full-sample experiment's family is its completed trials. A walk-forward or cross-validated experiment's is its fold series, joined when the windows tile the sample. A CPCV experiment's is one path, which the caller names. N is the family's members with a Sharpe ratio. The deflation leaves the flat members out; it is None if the selection is flat or fewer than two members remain. SPA tests the members whose relative performance varies and names the constant ones; it is None if fewer than two vary. The Reality Check takes the whole family. The assessment's identity covers the members each statistic left out.
technical_decisions.rationale: A statistic that refuses a member is right about it. The assessment keeps research's definitions rather than overriding them: what it cannot measure, it names. A constant relative performance is its own verdict -- the member beats the benchmark by its constant in every period, or by nothing -- so it needs no test. SPA's p-values remain those of the members it can studentize. A designed experiment's folds are the same candidates again, not further independent trials.
technical_decisions.compatibility: Additive: a new module, alphalab.lifecycle.assessment, and four exports. Research's statistics are unchanged, and nothing recorded before moves.
technical_decisions.record: docs/ADR/0073-validation-over-backtests.md, settled 11-14.
technical_decisions.tests: tests/integration/test_experiment_assessment.py (15): each design's family equals the ledger's series, joined. Every statistic equals research's own called by hand over the family, SPA's over the members left in. M3's bridge over the same trials, run again, gives the same PBO. Each refusal is held: another experiment's record, a path where none belongs or none named, a path out of range, windows that gap or overlap, fewer than two candidates, and a benchmark of the wrong length or not finite. The identity is pinned for three designs, and each choice moves it. tests/unit/lifecycle/test_assessment_members.py (5): the members left out, and the cases with no statistic.

technical_decisions.title: Selection-aware evidence: what EXPERIMENT evidence carries, and where the family-count refusal lives
technical_decisions.problem: ADR-0073 section 8 requires promotion to refuse EXPERIMENT evidence that does not state its family count. Four things were open: where the refusal lives, what the metrics are named, which fields are derived rather than supplied, and how a statistic the assessment could not compute is recorded.
technical_decisions.alternatives: The refusal: (a) at construction, in ValidationEvidence, which makes such evidence unrepresentable and a stored one fail to decode; (b) a policy option, so a policy that omits it lets a hidden search through; (c) in evaluate_policy, under every policy. The metrics: flat names under a prefix, since evidence metrics are a flat mapping of floats. An uncomputed statistic: a placeholder (0 or NaN), or left out.
technical_decisions.decision: (c): evaluate_policy fails EXPERIMENT evidence that does not state EXPERIMENT_FAMILY_METRIC (experiment.trials) as a whole number of trials, at least one, whatever the policy's thresholds and required method. evidence_from_experiment(spec, record, assessment, subject, produced_at) checks that the record is the experiment's and the assessment the record's. Its metrics are prefixed experiment.: trials, pbo, reality_check_p, SPA's three p-values, and the selection's sharpe, deflated_sharpe and deflated_sharpe_trials. The dataset is the experiment's dataset_id, the seed the experiment's, and source_id the assessment's identity. A statistic not computed is left out.
technical_decisions.rationale: Evidence records what was measured, and the gate is the policy. Putting the gate in every policy means no policy can forget it. A metric left out fails any threshold on it for want of the metric, as an undefined backtest metric has since v3.10, rather than passing on a placeholder.
technical_decisions.compatibility: Additive. ValidationMethod.EXPERIMENT is appended, and evidence_id_for hashes method.name, so no evidence identity moved; the persisted name is pinned. The new check touches only EXPERIMENT evidence, which no earlier release could produce.
technical_decisions.record: docs/ADR/0073-validation-over-backtests.md, settled 15.
technical_decisions.tests: tests/integration/test_selection_aware_promotion.py (14). The walk-forward reference experiment's evidence carries the family count (33) and the exact statistics, and a promotion on it passes. The same policy's thresholds are met by hand-built EXPERIMENT evidence, and its promotion is refused: the count absent, zero, negative, fractional, NaN, infinite or a boolean. Every other policy refuses it too, while BACKTEST evidence needs no count. A statistic left out fails for want of the metric. The evidence identity's rendering is pinned, and the evidence survives a lifecycle snapshot.

technical_decisions.title: EXPERIMENT evidence carries no class-3 value: the deflated Sharpe ratio is read from the assessment
technical_decisions.problem: TD-28 put the deflated Sharpe ratio among EXPERIMENT evidence's metrics. An evidence identity covers its metrics. The ratio runs through the normal CDF and quantile, which are host-libm arithmetic (class 3, ADR-0058), so one assessment could give two hosts two evidence identities. A backtest's evidence is kept host-independent: its CAGR is a correctly rounded Decimal power.
technical_decisions.alternatives: (a) Keep the ratio, and document a host-dependent evidence identity. (b) Compute the normal CDF and quantile on a class-2 path now. (c) Leave the ratio out of the metrics, read it from the assessment the evidence names, and track (b) as future work.
technical_decisions.decision: (c). EXPERIMENT evidence carries the family count, PBO, the Reality Check's and SPA's p-values (exact), the selection's Sharpe ratio (class 2) and the N of its deflation. The deflated Sharpe ratio is reported in the assessment. A class-2 normal CDF and quantile are ledger FUT-051 (v4.4).
technical_decisions.rationale: ADR-0058's rule: a value that enters an identity is computed on class 1 or 2 paths only, and a class-3 value is recorded beside an identity, never in it. (b) is numerical-foundation work, with its own error analysis and pins; it is not M5's.
technical_decisions.compatibility: EXPERIMENT evidence was added on this branch (a2903ae) and never released, so nothing stored moves.
technical_decisions.record: docs/ADR/0073-validation-over-backtests.md, settled 15 and its known limitation; ledger FUT-051.
technical_decisions.tests: tests/integration/test_selection_aware_promotion.py: the evidence carries no deflated Sharpe ratio. S-13 reads the ratio from the assessment, and gates the promotion on the exact statistics. test_every_adr_deferral_is_classified holds ADR-0073's limitation to FUT-051.

technical_decisions.title: ADR-0074 accepted: econometrics, its estimates, and the fitted half-life (OFE-007) reopened
technical_decisions.problem: GAP-11: no unit roots, cointegration, ARMA, VAR, GARCH or state space. The plan (H.3, WS-07, N6) asks for a pure econometrics package returning Estimates. It assigns no ADR number. D-V3 asks that each boundary reopening get its own ADR before its milestone, and OFE-007's boundary (a half-life is a model choice quoted as a measurement) waited for ADR-0058's estimation identity.
technical_decisions.alternatives: Methods inside research, or a package of their own beside common. A data identity the caller types, or one derived from the values. Defaults for lags, deterministic terms and bandwidths, or every choice stated. OFE-007 kept, or reopened as an estimate of a named model.
technical_decisions.decision: A pure alphalab.econometrics importing only common. Every fit is an Estimate; every test returns its statistic, the critical values with their source, the p-value with how it was computed, and its regression's Estimate. The data's identity is derived from the values. Every choice is stated. Results are classed by ADR-0058: least-squares statistics, response-surface critical values and Johansen's eigenvalues are class 2 and in identities; likelihood fits, Johansen's statistics and normal-based p-values are class 3, beside them. MacKinnon's 2010 response surfaces and 1994 p-value approximations, and KPSS's table, are published constants held to their tables. OFE-007 is reopened as the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck fit: a class-2 AR(1) estimate and a class-3 continuous-time estimate with the half-life and its standard error; a coefficient outside (0, 1) is refused. S-02's screen counts every pair, states its correction, and feeds a ledgered experiment whose runner fits on its own window.
technical_decisions.rationale: A model's choices change its answer, so they are stated, as ADR-0054 states the selection statistics'. A typed identity is only as true as the typing (ADR-0017). A half-life is reportable once it says what model it estimates and how precisely.
technical_decisions.compatibility: Additive: a new package and a research function. factor_library.decay and every identity are unchanged.
technical_decisions.record: docs/ADR/0074-econometrics-time-series-estimation-with-an-identity.md.
technical_decisions.tests: M6's: known-DGP recovery for every model, MacKinnon's published critical values reproduced to three decimals, the refusals, the GARCH and Johansen budgets, and S-02's screening stage.

technical_decisions.title: ADR-0075 accepted: statistical regime models (OFE-010) reopened
technical_decisions.problem: OFE-010 kept hidden Markov and Markov-switching models out because an estimation model with a fitting window had no identity. ADR-0058 supplied one. D-V3 asks for an ADR per reopening.
technical_decisions.alternatives: Keep the boundary; reopen in research beside the declared rules; or reopen in econometrics as estimators returning Estimates, with the declared rules unchanged. Automatic restarts from several points, or one start per fit. A variance floor for a collapsing state, or a refusal.
technical_decisions.decision: Reopen in econometrics.regimes: a univariate GaussianHMM by Baum-Welch (scaled forward-backward), and a MarkovSwitchingRegression by Hamilton's filter and Kim's smoother. K, the start (explicit or a named rule), the tolerance and the limit are stated. One start per fit, with no hidden search. A collapsing state, too little data and non-convergence are refused. States are labelled by ascending mean (ascending variance for the regression). Everything passes through exp and log, class 3, beside the identity, which covers the problem. Multivariate emissions are deferred as FUT-052.
technical_decisions.rationale: The boundary's reason is met. The declared rules remain the engine's regime layer, and a decoded path is labels a caller may hand to research. A restart loop hidden inside an estimator would be an uncounted search.
technical_decisions.compatibility: Additive. research.regimes and every identity are unchanged.
technical_decisions.record: docs/ADR/0075-statistical-regime-models-with-an-identity.md; ledger FUT-052.
technical_decisions.tests: Simulated regime recovery, and forward-backward probabilities checked against exact hand computation on small chains.

technical_decisions.title: PC-07 on hosted runners: the trace's chain computed in batches, byte for byte
technical_decisions.problem: The M6 writer change, approved by the owner, measured 10.9 to 12.8 percent on the reference machine. Hosted runners read series and trace at 11.9 to 16.8 percent on CPython 3.12 (benchmarks run 43788977726, ce20731, Ubuntu). That is 16.8 at a trade on every eighth record: a failed PC-07 gate. They read up to 13.1 percent on 3.13 and 14.7 on 3.14. Measured layer by layer in the run's own loop, most of the trace's cost was its serialization, at about twice what the same work cost measured alone: it ran between two of the run's steps, on code and data the step had pushed out of the processor's caches.
technical_decisions.alternatives: (a) Narrow the trace, or raise the ceiling: excluded by PC-07 and the owner. (b) Judge the benchmark on more samples: a change to the measurement, not to the code; not taken. (c) More per-value work saved: skipping a log the run left as it was and reading a grown one in one call cut the capture's cost 6 to 11 percent; a plan of field writers per type signature measured no faster and was dropped. (d) Compute the chain in batches of steps: the same links, in the same order, computed with warm caches.
technical_decisions.decision: (c)'s skips and one-call reads, and (d). The trace takes each step's entries as the step ends, and chains 64 steps at a time. finish chains what remains. When the run fails, run_captured chains what the trace took before re-raising, so a step the trace cannot write fails the capture before anything the run did after it. Batches of 16 gave about half the gain; 256 no more than 64.
technical_decisions.rationale: Measured in the run's own loop against ce20731, interleaved, fastest of 7: the capture's cost fell 20 to 37 percent at the four densities. The benchmark itself, run twice, read series and trace at 7.6 to 8.9 percent on the reference machine, from 10.9 to 12.8. The bytes are unchanged. Every payload of 1,608 steps was compared with ce20731's writer and with serialize, and 11,736 steps of the capture tests with serialize. The pinned trace identities hold.
technical_decisions.compatibility: No identity, format or public name moves. A run holds at most 64 steps' entries until they are chained; retention bounds its memory as before. A step the trace cannot write still fails run_captured with the same SerializationError: at the end of its batch, at finish, or when the run fails, before the run's own failure.
technical_decisions.record: docs/ADR/0055 (settled point 6, departures, known limitation); ledger LIM-013; ROADMAP; CHANGELOG; benchmarks/benchmark_capture.py.
technical_decisions.tests: tests/unit/backtesting/test_capture_writer.py holds the writer to serialize for every kind of value, a batched chain to the step-by-step chain across batch boundaries, a step's failure before a later failure of the run, and a failed batch to one failure. tests/unit/common/test_append_log.py covers _since. The pinned trace identities hold. Seven deliberate faults were each caught by the test written for them.

technical_decisions.title: The benchmarks run on Linux and macOS, and every benchmark runs after one fails
technical_decisions.problem: PC-07's verdict is read from the benchmarks workflow, which ran on Ubuntu alone: three cells, where the quality gates hold six. Its first failing benchmark stopped its job. On CPython 3.12 the capture benchmark's failure hid every benchmark after it twice: at M5's checkpoint, and again on ce20731.
technical_decisions.alternatives: Keep Linux alone; add macOS. Stop at the first failure; run every benchmark and fail the job at the end. Bound each benchmark with GNU timeout, which macOS lacks; or with Python's subprocess.

technical_decisions.rationale: A benchmark's verdict, PC-07's among them, is read on both systems the quality gates hold. A failure should hide nothing measured after it, as one failing cell hides no other.

technical_decisions.title: A design with a dependent column is refused as ill-conditioned: one-sided Jacobi settles on rounding noise (NUM-018)
technical_decisions.problem: least_squares documents that a rank-deficient design is refused with IllConditionedError. For a regressor beside a multiple of itself it often raised that the singular values had not converged. Householder QR leaves the two columns exactly parallel in its triangular factor. Rotated together they leave a column of rounding noise, and the relative criterion |gamma| <= eps sqrt(alpha beta) cycles on noise: rotating noise against the other columns makes new noise. In 400 random designs [1, x, c x], 181 failed so.
technical_decisions.alternatives: (a) Bound the condition number by the factor's diagonal before the singular values: it changes the reported condition of designs refused today. (b) Catch the non-convergence in least_squares and refuse by that bound: leaves singular_values failing on the same matrices. (c) A looser criterion throughout: moves pinned values. (d) The strict criterion alone first; only for a matrix that has not settled after 64 sweeps, leave a column within the sweeps' own backward-error bound of zero out of further rotations.
technical_decisions.decision: (d). Every matrix that meets the strict criterion gets it alone, the same operations in the same order. After 64 sweeps, a column whose norm is at most 8 n (k + 1) eps ||A||_F, with k the 128 sweeps the call may make (Higham, Lemma 19.9, the bound M2's tests state), is no longer rotated, and its norm is reported as its singular value. A matrix that still does not settle is refused as before.
technical_decisions.rationale: Zeroing such a column moves the matrix by less than the error the sweeps already carry, so the values reported are those of a matrix the computation cannot tell from the input. The design is then refused as least_squares documents.
technical_decisions.compatibility: No converging input changes by a bit: every pinned value of the linear algebra holds. A dependent design that raised AlphaLabValidationError now raises IllConditionedError, a subclass of it.
technical_decisions.record: Ledger NUM-018; CHANGELOG (Fixed).
technical_decisions.tests: tests/unit/common/test_linalg.py: the captured factor's singular values, held to their closed form in 50-digit Decimal within the bound; 200 dependent designs each refused as ill-conditioned (90 raised the non-convergence before). technical_decisions.title: PC-07's verdict on six cells: the capture judged on nine samples, macOS running the capture benchmark
technical_decisions.problem: Benchmarks run 43794814136 on 61b4793 read series and trace at 7.0 to 10.5 percent on hosted Linux under CPython 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14. On hosted macOS, measured for the first time (TD-33), it read figures that cannot all be true. On 3.12 the series alone was +10.0 percent where series and trace read +6.7, and series and trace read +25.3 at one density. On 3.13 the series read -2.4 percent at one density, and +23.8 against +22.2 for series and trace at another. Two cells exceeded the ceiling: a failed gate on each, recorded as such. The same runners failed two ceilings never judged there before, on readings of the same kind: an order book's scaling at 3.07x on one cell and 1.85x, below linear, on the next; a reused worker's overhead at 15.3 percent on one and 3.9 on another.
technical_decisions.alternatives: (a) Raise or relax the ceiling, or judge macOS as information only: excluded, as a change to the gate. (b) Revert macOS: loses the six cells the owner asked for. (c) Judge on more samples: the same estimator, the fastest of interleaved samples, with more chances at a quiet moment. The harness's default cannot rise, because the experiments benchmark would exceed its 900-second bound. (d) A paired median of ratios: a new estimator; not taken.
technical_decisions.decision: (c) for the capture benchmark: the fastest of nine samples. macOS cells run the capture benchmark alone, PC-07's verdict on both systems. Linux runs every benchmark, as it did before TD-33. The limits, the workload and the trace's coverage are unchanged, and every result above the ceiling is recorded as a failed gate.
technical_decisions.rationale: The capture's cost is about a tenth of a run, judged against a ceiling at a seventh, so a minimum inflated by a few percent decides the verdict. The fastest of three left every sample of one workload in a slow phase of the runner, and figures that contradict each other cannot be a measurement of the code.
technical_decisions.compatibility: No code changes. The capture benchmark takes about three times as long, about 3 to 5 minutes a cell.

technical_decisions.title: PC-07 judged on the median of paired ratios, and a self-contradicting measurement fails
technical_decisions.problem: On nine samples (benchmarks run 43818953549, 0095775) hosted macOS still read figures that cannot all be true. On 3.12 series and trace read +16.8% at a trade on every record, a failed PC-07 gate, with the series alone at -5.6% at one density and above series and trace at another. On 3.14 series and trace read -1.4% and -6.7%, and the series alone +10.9%, over its budget. On 3.13 series and trace read -7.9% and -5.1%, and the old verdict passed that cell though it proved nothing. Comparing each workload's fastest sample compares samples the runner ran at different speeds.
technical_decisions.alternatives: (a) More samples: nine already failed, and the experiments benchmark bounds the job's time. (b) Judge macOS as information only: a change to the gate, for the owner. (c) The median of paired ratios: each round runs the workloads back to back, so a slow phase or a slower core that covers the round scales numerator and denominator alike, and the median discards a round that one fell into alone. (d) Fail a measurement that contradicts itself rather than read a verdict from it.
technical_decisions.decision: (c) and (d). _stable_timing gains rounds(), the per-round times; fastest() is the minimum over them, unchanged for every other benchmark. The capture benchmark judges the median of each round's ratio over nine rounds and prints each ratio's range across the rounds. It fails a density as INCONSISTENT when the series alone reads below -2 percent or series and trace below the series alone by more than 2 points, beside any limit exceeded. The limits, the workload and the trace's coverage are unchanged.
technical_decisions.rationale: A benchmark that can read a capture cheaper than none cannot be the evidence of a ceiling either way. On the reference machine the paired median reads what the fastest-of-N read: series and trace 7.5 to 8.7 percent, the series 1.2 to 3.6.
technical_decisions.compatibility: No code changes. fastest() runs the same samples in the same order.

plan_changes.change: Plan H.1 names cyclic Jacobi as the symmetric eigensystem's algorithm. common.linalg.symmetric_eigensystem is Householder tridiagonalization and implicit QL (Bowdler, Martin, Reinsch and Wilkinson's tql2) instead; the thin SVD stays one-sided Jacobi as H.1 names it. plan_changes.reason: The two parts of the plan could not both hold: cyclic Jacobi was written first and measured at 147.5 s for a 500 x 500 eigensystem against WS-03's 30 s budget; Householder and implicit QL, equally backward stable with orthonormal vectors, measured 20.7 s. Of an algorithm and a budget, the budget is the acceptance criterion.

plan_changes.decision: Owner approved, 2026-11-15 (proposed under delegated authority, TD-17). On 2026-11-16 the owner approved the M6 output-identical change to the trace's writer (466d350, amended as ce20731 with its certificate corrected), the limits unchanged: the approval is of the change, and the gate passes only by a hosted measurement within the limits. A result above 15 percent stays a failed gate; the remedy is further output-identical optimisation, and a decision beyond the approved limits goes to the owner (TD-32).
plan_changes.change: Plan K.1 budgets the capture at 10 percent of the run's time; that target stays the plan's record. Approved limits: the return series alone at most 10 percent, and the series with its complete economic-history trace at most 15 percent, measured at several trade densities, sparse and dense. 15 percent is a ceiling, not a target: optimisation continues wherever it costs nothing in correctness or research integrity, and trace coverage, canonical form and reproducibility are never weakened to meet a budget. A combined result above 15 percent is a failed performance gate, brought to the owner for a new decision; the limit is never raised silently. benchmarks/benchmark_capture.py enforces both limits.
plan_changes.reason: Measured on a strategy that does no work of its own, the case where every ratio is largest: the series costs 1 to 4 percent of the run, and series and trace together 12.6 to 14.4 percent at a trade on every record and on every second, fourth and eighth, where digest_run costs 76 to 105 percent. Unlike PC-06, no design met 10 percent. The canonical serialization was made 2.7 times faster, byte for byte. Narrowing the trace would still miss: with a trade on every eighth record it costs 12.2 percent without the order events and 11.4 percent without the equity points, because most of its cost is the work it does every step. Covering less would make the trace identify less of the history. The cost is a fixed amount per step, so it is a smaller share of a run whose strategy computes anything (LIM-013).
